answer: An agent economy can make reputation portable only after an identity posts a refundable bond, then slash that bond when independent counterparties prove fraud through signed transaction receipts. Creating a thousand aliases no longer creates a thousand trusted histories: each must lock real capital, and laundering reputation across them risks forfeiting the bond. The pearl of the design is that verification follows costly behavior, not names; a relic credential or kernel label alone earns no trust. The attacker pays capital and loses it when caught.
